nodes.title: Groups that move points
nodes.text: A permutation group $G$ on $\{1, \dots, n\}$ **acts** on the points: each $g \in G$ sends a point $i$ to $g(i)$. The **orbit** of $i$ is every point $G$ can send it to, $G \cdot i = \{ g(i) : g \in G \}$. $G$ is **transitive** when there is one orbit: every point can be sent to every other.

nodes.code:
C = CyclicPermutationGroup(4)   # turns a square: 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 1
H = PermutationGroup([(1,2), (3,4)])   # swaps 1 and 2, and 3 and 4
D = DihedralGroup(4)   # every symmetry of a square, corners 1, 2, 3, 4
S = SymmetricGroup(4)   # every permutation of 1, 2, 3, 4
[C.orbits(), H.orbits()]

nodes.title: The turns
nodes.text: Is $C$, the rotations of a square, transitive on its corners?
nodes.check: answer == ('yes' if C.is_transitive() else 'no') or 'A turn takes $1$ to $2$, two turns to $3$, three to $4$: where can $1$ not go?'

nodes.title: Two swaps
hints: Start with the point $1$: where can $H$ send it?

hints.code: 'The orbit of $1$ is $\\{%s\\}$, and the orbit of $3$ is $\\{%s\\}$.' % (', '.join(map(str, H.orbit(1))), ', '.join(map(str, H.orbit(3))))

nodes.title: Orbits split the points
nodes.text: The orbits of $G$ split $\{1, \dots, n\}$ into parts. $C$ has one part, so it is transitive; $H$ has two, $\{1, 2\}$ and $\{3, 4\}$, so it is not.

nodes.title: Orbit and stabilizer
nodes.text: $S$ has $24$ elements and is transitive on $4$ points. How many elements of $S$ fix the point $1$?
nodes.check: answer == S.stabilizer(1).order() or ('No: %s is not $24 / 4$.' % answer if answer != 24 // 4 else False)
hints: $|G| = |G \cdot i| \cdot |G_i|$, where $G_i$ is the stabilizer of $i$: the elements with $g(i) = i$.

nodes.title: The orbit-stabilizer theorem
nodes.text: For every point $i$, $|G| = |G \cdot i| \cdot |G_i|$. So a transitive $G$ on $n$ points has $|G_i| = |G| / n$.

nodes.title: Transitive, but in blocks
nodes.text: A transitive group can still keep points together. $D$ sends opposite corners of the square to opposite corners: $\{1, 3\}$ and $\{2, 4\}$ are **blocks**. A transitive group with no blocks but the trivial ones is **primitive**.

nodes.title: Primitive?
nodes.text: Is $D$, the symmetries of the square, primitive?

hints.code: 'Try $\\{%s\\}$: $D$ sends it to a block of the same size, and those blocks never overlap.' % ', '.join(map(str, D.blocks_all()[0]))

nodes.title: In your own words
nodes.text: What does it mean for a group to act **transitively**?

decide.name: confuses-transitive-with-two-transitive
decide.about: Says any ordered pair of distinct points can be sent to any other, the two points moved simultaneously by one group element: that is 2-transitive, more than transitive.

decide.name: thinks-transitive-means-abelian
decide.about: Mixes it up with a commutative group.

decide.name: thinks-every-element-moves-every-point
decide.about: Says each element moves every point, rather than the group taking each point to each point.

nodes.title: 2-transitive is more
nodes.text: $G$ is **2-transitive** when it sends any ordered pair of distinct points to any other, the two moved simultaneously by one group element. $S$ is; $C$ is transitive but not 2-transitive: no rotation fixes $1$ and moves $2$.
